title: Android TextView: combining accent width
purpose: Check that a combining accent does not add a separate character width to a wrap-content Android XML TextView.
changes: The shared text-width fallback now counts each grapheme cluster once, so combining marks and joined emoji do not add a separate advance for every code point. ASCII keeps its fast path.
steps: At the top of the example, compare the two colored boxes: one contains e with a combining acute accent, and the other contains a plain e.
The boxes should have the same width; the accent should sit over the first letter.
Choose OK if it looks correct, or Reject with details and your device.
expected: The combining accent does not make the first wrap-content box wider than the plain-letter box.
limits: This improves width estimation but does not implement full Unicode shaping, kerning or actual non-ASCII glyph measurement. Android device and font parity remain unverified.
validation: The full libbhoo Rust suite and 156 XML importer tests passed; dedicated tests cover combining marks, joined emoji and letter spacing.
A 320 × 650 browser pixel test verified the two example backgrounds have matching widths.
